Donna di 69 anni, ex fumatrice (criteri: 69-year-old woman, former smoker (NLST entry criteria: age 55-74, at least 30 pack-years, quit less than 15 years ago). Screening with low-dose CT without contrast. Third annual exam (T2). The baseline CT from two years earlier (T0) is available, judged positive for a nodule of the right lower lobe; the intermediate follow-up (T1) had described it as unchanged. The exam dates are conventional.
Confronta con la TC basale: com'è il nod: Compare with the baseline CT: what is the right lower lobe nodule like and which Lung-RADS category do you assign today?
Nello screening la stabilità nel tempo è:
In screening, stability over time is the best criterion of benignity for a solid nodule. This nodule of about 7-9 mm in the right lower lobe, at baseline, fell into Lung-RADS category 3-4A (depending on the measurement) and had been judged positive. At the annual follow-ups it has not changed: according to Lung-RADS v2022 a category 3 or 4A nodule that remains unchanged at follow-up is downgraded (4A first to 3, then to 2): stable for two years it is category 2 and the patient returns to annual screening.

The small differences between the measurements (9, 7, 9 mm) are due to variability: 3.2 mm slices, partial volume, measurement on different images. To say "growth" requires an increase of at least 1.5 mm in mean diameter (Lung-RADS) or, better, a volumetric measurement.

Pitfall of the baseline: at the right base, in front of the heart, the dome of the liver cut tangentially looks like a round mass. It must always be followed on the subsequent images.

Outcome: in the collection the patient had no lung cancer in the roughly 6.7 years of follow-up.

Low-dose chest CT without contrast (screening).

In the posterior subpleural portion of the right lower lobe, solid nodule of about 9 mm, with sharp margins, with a small adjacent calcified granuloma. No other significant nodules. No adenopathy, no effusion.

Conclusions: 9 mm solid nodule of the right lower lobe: positive screening, short-term follow-up CT. (Teaching report written for the case, not the original report.)
